Company Profile and Chatbot Scope Company ID: NOVA-COMP-001 | Document version 3.0 Company background NovaTech Electronics is a fictional consumer-electronics retailer created as a realistic sample knowledge base for a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot. Every brand name, product identifier, price, specification, service detail, and policy in this document is invented for software development and testing. It must not be presented as a real commercial offer. Customer promise The fictional company focuses on helping customers select compatible technology, understand trade-offs, and solve common problems safely. A good answer should explain why an option fits the customer's stated needs, mention important limitations, and avoid exaggerating performance or compatibility. Customer groups The sample audience includes university students, office workers, remote employees, families, gamers, content creators, and small businesses.

These customers have different priorities: a student may prioritize cost and portability; a developer may need memory and storage; a family may value ease of use; and a designer may need display detail and graphics capability. Example support hours: Sunday–Thursday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM Egypt time, excluding public holidays. The .example domain and phone are placeholders and are not real contact channels. What the chatbot can do The chatbot can explain documented product features, compare products, summarize the sample policies, guide customers through safe basic troubleshooting, and ask clarifying questions. It can cite product IDs and distinguish known information from unknown details. It should answer in the language used by the customer when possible.

What the chatbot cannot do Unless a real external system is connected, the chatbot cannot check current inventory, track a parcel, create or cancel an order, charge a payment method, approve a refund, verify warranty status, or see repair progress. It must never pretend that these actions have been completed. Grounding and uncertainty When information is missing, use a direct phrase such as: “The NovaTech demo knowledge base does not specify that detail.” Then name the missing fact and suggest what should be checked. Do not infer water resistance, benchmark scores, certifications, included accessories, or exact arrival dates from a product name. RAG Pipeline Notes, Metadata, and Glossary Content type: Implementation reference | Document ID: NOVA-KB-003 Suggested chunk metadata Store fields such as source_file, document_version, page_number, section_title, content_type, category, product_id, policy_id, and language alongside each chunk. Product chunks should carry their product ID; policy chunks should carry a policy ID; FAQ and evaluation chunks should be marked separately. Chunking approach Start by splitting on page and section headings so that a product specification or policy condition stays together. Then split unusually long sections into smaller pieces. A practical experiment might compare chunks of approximately 300–500 tokens with modest overlap, but the best settings depend on the embedding model, retrieval method, and test queries.

Embedding consistency Use the same embedding model for all document chunks and user queries in one vector index. If you change embedding models or vector dimensions, rebuild the index consistently instead of mixing vectors from different spaces. Store the original text and metadata so retrieved evidence can be shown and debugged. Retrieval and generation At query time, embed the question, retrieve the most relevant chunks, optionally rerank them, and provide the evidence to the language model. The system prompt should instruct the model to answer from retrieved context, preserve product IDs, distinguish fictional examples from live information, and say when evidence is missing. Evaluation plan Create a test set of direct product lookups, price questions, product comparisons, policy questions, troubleshooting queries, multi-hop questions, and unanswerable questions.

Measure retrieval recall, answer correctness, groundedness, and hallucination rate. Inspect retrieved chunks when an answer fails. Glossary RAG means Retrieval-Augmented Generation: retrieving relevant source text before generating a response. A chunk is a segment of source text. An embedding is a numerical vector representation of text. A vector database stores vectors and supports similarity search. Metadata is structured information attached to a chunk. Retrieval selects relevant passages; generation produces the final response. Operational cautions The file is a fictional demo, not a real product database. Prices and policies should be updated from an authoritative source in a real deployment. Never expose private customer data in retrieval chunks.
